cards.back: Messenger who brings revelation and a new law.
Messengers.
Prophet who receives revelation but does not bring a new law.
Prophets.
All messengers are prophets, but not all prophets are messengers. A prophet receives revelation with no new law; a messenger receives revelation plus a new law.
Prophets were human beings (not divine). They ate, drank, fell ill, and died like other humans.
They never claimed divinity; they conveyed Allah’s message only by His permission.
To guide people back to worshipping Allah alone. They are role models in character and behavior.
Believers believe in Allah, His Angels, His Books, and His Messengers, and make no distinction between His messengers.

cards.front: Unified divine mission of prophets and messengers
cards.back: Call to Tawheed (monotheism) and teach Salah, Zakah, and righteousness.

cards.front: How revelation is received by prophets
cards.back: Revelation was received through inspiration, from behind a veil, or via angel Jibreel (Shura: 51).
A miracle—divine proof given by Allah, not magic.
Miracles are divine proof, not magic, and they are given according to people’s culture/time.
Fire became cool (Al-Anbiyaa: 69).
Staff became a real serpent and the sea split (Taha: 69–70).
Born without a father; healed blind/lepers, raised dead (Al-Imran: 49).
She-camel emerged from the mountain (Al-A‘raf: 73).
The Qur’an itself, unmatched in eloquence (Al-Isra: 88).
To prove the truthfulness of prophets and to strengthen people’s faith.

cards.front: Why prophets are moral role models
cards.back: They have excellent character and teach patience, perseverance, and righteousness.
Monotheism.
Infallibility—prophets are sinless in conveying Allah’s message (never lie, forget, or alter revelation).

cards.front: Do prophets make mistakes in delivering revelation?
cards.back: No. Their human errors in worldly matters are minor, unintentional, and immediately corrected by Allah; the corrections are preserved in the Qur’an.
Surat Abasa (blind man incident).
Hasty judgment corrected.
Left his people early, swallowed by whale, repented.

cards.front: Number of prophets named in the Qur’an
cards.back: 25 named in the Qur’an (Adam to Muhammad ﷺ).
124,000 prophets and 315 messengers in total.
Prophets of high determination and power. Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, Muhammad ﷺ

cards.front: Muhammad ﷺ significance in the notes
cards.back: Sent as mercy to the worlds and universally to all humanity; also the Seal of Prophethood.

cards.front: Muhammad ﷺ finality meaning (Imam Muslim example)
cards.back: Like a house completed except one brick; “I am this final brick, and I am the final prophet.”
Independent thinking (prophets may use it in worldly matters; if they err, they are corrected by Allah).
Best character traits, obedience, humility, repentance—and gratitude for Allah’s guidance through prophets.
